messages:
Rita (Support): FYI ACME Prod reported p99 spikes for embeddings/generation since ~04:10 UTC after maintenance window. Customer says 99th went from ~200ms -> ~1.8s. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/ACME-123
Alice (SRE): looking now. p95 jumped 120ms -> 450ms, p99 ~1.8s. Any infra changes during window?
deploy-bot: deployment redwood-runtime@v2.3.1 rolled out to eu-west-1 at 04:05 UTC (nvidia-driver bumped 525.60.13 -> 530.12.01).
Bob (Infra): we also staged GPU firmware 2.1.4 and host kernel preempt backport in that same window for eu-west-1.
Claire (Runtime): Observed NVMe qdepth waiting increase on inference hosts and KV cache miss tail latency rising. Could be IO contention with new driver/firmware combo.
Rita (Support): Customer provided a simple repro: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/embeds -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"input": "test"}' -w "time_total:%{time_total}\n'` — they see sporadic high times.
Mike (Oncall): Can someone ssh to eu-w-3a-07 and run `iostat -x 1 3` and `sudo perf record -a`? I'll grab baseline from monitoring.
Alice (SRE): grabbing dmesg from eu-w-3a-07, snippet shows repeated nvme timeouts around 04:06-04:08:
```[04:07:10] nvme0: I/O 12345 queued, timeout
[04:07:10] nvme0: aborting command
[04:07:11] nvme0: reset controller
```
Bob (Infra): NVMe firmware 6.3 was rolled during capacity fixes earlier today in that AZ. I haven't seen these timeouts before with 525 driver + fw6.3 combo. Might be regression.
Claire (Runtime): Short mitigation: add routing rule to prefer dedicated pool `dedicated-eu-west-l` for embeddings (-> reduces pressure on shared nodes) and fallback to older runtime variant. I'll push a 20% split immediately to reduce customer impact.
Rita (Support): Communicated to ACME that we're routing some traffic away and investigating; they reported immediate improvement on routed requests.
Mike (Oncall): On eu-w-3a-07 I applied quick IO tuning to reduce tail: 
```# reduce per-queue depth
sudo sh -c 'echo 64 > /sys/class/nvme/nvme0/queue_depth'
# set scheduler to mq-deadline
sudo bash -c 'echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler'
```
Claire (Runtime): Also constrained inference threads via cpuset so they avoid noisy host scheduling after the preempt backport. Applied to eu-w-3a-0[6-9].
Alice (SRE): Plan: reproduce locally with synthetic load, run a 2x2 matrix (driver 525/530 x nvme-fw 6.2/6.3) to isolate. If confirmed, rollback driver on a canary rack and monitor p99.
Bob (Infra): I'll coordinate a canary rollback on one rack later this hour and open vendor ticket with NVMe vendor (attach dmesg & iostat).
Claire (Runtime): Saved repro steps and curl snippets + logs to /var/log/redwood/incidents/1719002468/repro.txt.
Rita (Support): ACME says routed requests show p95 improvement. I'll keep them updated and keep this thread for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
Mike (Oncall): Action items: nightly regression matrix for driver/fw combos (assign: Bob/Alice), keep routing rule in place until canary confirms rollback/patch.
Rita (Support): Thanks everyone — marking as ongoing. Will escalate to SEV if rollback doesn't improve within 2 hours.
